artworks.title: Ismene and Antigone Plead with Theseus
artworks.description: Abildgaard's oil in the Statens Museum for Kunst shows the Theban sisters before Theseus, begging for their father's resting place at Colonus. Ismene stands with Antigone as co-suppliant — not the cautious foil of Sophocles' Antigone alone, but a daughter still pleading in the wake of Oedipus.

artworks.title: Oedipus Condemns Polynices (with Ismene and Antigone)
artworks.description: Baschet's academic canvas stages the Colonus curse: blind Oedipus turns on Polynices while Ismene and Antigone frame the scene. The quieter sister is present as witness — filial piety caught between brothers already doomed.

artworks.title: Tydeus and Ismene (Corinthian amphora, Louvre E640)
artworks.description: A Corinthian black-figure amphora in the Louvre names Ismene beside Tydeus — a rare archaic image of the Theban princess in the cycle of the Seven against Thebes. The vase preserves a darker local strand in which Ismene herself falls in the war her brothers began.

artworks.title: Antigone and Ismene
artworks.description: Kiwitz's 1931 print pairs the sisters as a modern woodcut dialogue — Antigone's resolve set against Ismene's caution. The image keeps Sophocles' two voices in one frame, Ismene no longer a footnote but the necessary other half of the argument.

films.title: Antigone
films.description: Javellas keeps Ismene as the sister who will not dig: caution against Antigone's fire, then late courage when the sentence is already fixed.

music.title: Antigone
music.description: Honegger gives Ismene the voice of survival — the sister who argues for life while Antigone chooses the grave.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Jean Anouilh
popCulture.description: Anouilh's Ismene is the reasonable sister under Occupation logic — she loves Antigone and still cannot bring herself to break the law.
